small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with smaller BLOCK_P (32, 64) since total_pooled = PD*PH*PW = 16*16*16 = 4096 per (n,oc) — small BLOCK_P with more programs may better saturate the 2048 (N*OC) grid; also try num_warps=2.
- Reorder the reduction loops so the IC loop is innermost-vectorized: hoist x_off base computation outside `ic` and fold IC into a tl.arange so the 3 input channels load as a small vector; this also lets weights be loaded once per (kd,kh,kw) as a (IC,) vector reused across BLOCK_P lanes.
- Grid expansion: split each (n,oc) over multiple pooled-tile programs and atomically accumulate the partial sum (or do a second tiny reduction kernel) — current grid is only 2048 programs for a 16k-SM-cycle workload, so spatial-parallelism is the bottleneck.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a two-stage design: (1) a scatter-add ConvTranspose3d kernel producing the full (N,OC,OD,OH,OW) tensor in channels-last layout, fused with `*scale`; (2) a fused maxpool→global-avg→clamp reduction kernel. The current gather formulation recomputes the same input contributions MK³=8 times per output cell because each pooled output revisits overlapping conv outputs — this is ~8× redundant work versus scatter.
- Alternative: implement convT as input-centric scatter — one program per (N, IC-tile, ID,IH,IW tile) computes the outer product with the (OC,KD,KH,KW) weight slice and atomic-adds (or block-accumulates in shared mem) into the output grid; then fuse pool+avg+clamp. This matches the "ConvTranspose3d as scatter-add" skill rule and removes the modular-arithmetic `id_r==0` mask overhead currently burned inside the gather.
- Increase parallelism granularity: launch grid of (N*OC, pooled-tile) and have each program reduce a chunk of pooled outputs, then do a tl.atomic_add of the partial sum into out[n,oc]. With N*OC=2048 the current kernel under-occupies the 128 SMs once each program does 4096 pooled cells × 27 kernel taps × 3 IC of work.
